title: fix(linux/gtk4): SIGSEGV on Ubuntu 24.04 / WebKitGTK 2.52+ — use-after-free of SoupMessageHeaders
body:
Summary

  All Wails v3 GTK4 apps crash immediately on Ubuntu 24.04 (WebKitGTK 6.0, libsoup-3.0 version 2.52.3) with a SIGSEGV inside soup_message_headers_iter_next. The crash is a use-after-free in Wails' own code — not a system bug. One line fix.

  Environment

  - Wails v3.0.0-alpha.96, GTK4 path (no -tags gtk3)
  - Ubuntu 24.04, libwebkitgtk-6.0-4 version 2.52.3, libsoup-3.0
  - Wayland or X11 session

  Reproduction

  Any default Wails GTK4 app crashes on launch:

  Platform Info: GTK=4.14.5 WebKitGTK=2.52.3
  [AssetFileServerFS] Handling request url=/index.html file=index.html
  SIGSEGV: segmentation violation
  signal arrived during cgo execution
    g_application_run → g_main_context_iteration → (libgio) → (libwebkitgtk-6.0)
    → soup_message_headers_iter_next  ← CRASH

  GDB backtrace:
  #0  soup_message_headers_iter_next () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsoup-3.0.so.0
  #1  ?? () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwebkitgtk-6.0.so.4
  #2  ?? () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libwebkitgtk-6.0.so.4
  #3-#10 libgio / libglib (async I/O callbacks)
  #11 g_application_run ()
  #12 _Cfunc_g_application_run (CGO boundary)

  Root cause

  In internal/assetserver/webview/webkit_linux.go, webkit_uri_scheme_request_finish creates a SoupMessageHeaders, passes it to
  webkit_uri_scheme_response_set_http_headers, then immediately frees it with defer:

  // BEFORE (buggy):
  hdrs := C.soup_message_headers_new(C.SOUP_MESSAGE_HEADERS_RESPONSE)
  defer C.soup_message_headers_unref(hdrs)   // ← frees memory WebKit still holds
  // ...
  C.webkit_uri_scheme_response_set_http_headers(resp, hdrs)

  webkit_uri_scheme_response_set_http_headers has a (transfer full) GObject annotation — it takes ownership of hdrs and will unref it when the response is finalized. Wails' defer frees the same object immediately when the Go function returns, while WebKit still holds the pointer. When WebKit later iterates the headers via soup_message_headers_iter_next, it accesses freed memory → SIGSEGV.

  Fix

  Remove the defer soup_message_headers_unref — WebKit owns the object from the moment webkit_uri_scheme_response_set_http_headers is called.

  internal/assetserver/webview/webkit_linux.go:

```
  -     hdrs := C.soup_message_headers_new(C.SOUP_MESSAGE_HEADERS_RESPONSE)
  -     defer C.soup_message_headers_unref(hdrs)
  -     for name, values := range header {
  +     // webkit_uri_scheme_response_set_http_headers takes (transfer full) ownership
  +     // of the SoupMessageHeaders — WebKit will unref it; do not call unref here.
  +     hdrs := C.soup_message_headers_new(C.SOUP_MESSAGE_HEADERS_RESPONSE)
  +     for name, values := range header {   

```
  Verification

  Tested on Ubuntu 24.04 + WebKitGTK 2.52.3 with a minimal Wails v3 app (30 lines, no app logic). Without fix: crashes immediately every time. With fix: window opens and renders correctly.

  Notes

  The crash manifests as "signal arrived during cgo execution" which led to extensive investigation of Go signal-handling (SA_ONSTACK, JSC_SIGNAL_FOR_GC). The real cause is unrelated to signals — it is a straightforward use-after-free. The misleading Go panic message appears because SIGSEGV fires inside C code (g_application_run) during CGO execution.

-------------
Root cause investigation and fix were found with the assistance of Claude. The debugging process involved: running GDB on the crashing binary to identify soup_message_headers_iter_next as the crash site, ruling out signal-handling theories (SA_ONSTACK, JSC_SIGNAL_FOR_GC) via targeted tests, and tracing the bad pointer back to the premature soup_message_headers_unref in Wails' own response writer.
